serves: Pio Duran (Albay); Lucena (Quezon); Calbayog (Samar); Bugui Point
operators: Starhorse Shipping Lines; Silverstone Goldrich Shipping
facilities: One berth - not viable for RoRo
notes: AROROY PORT IS NOT A RoRo PORT and MARINA says so plainly; it also records that passengers and shippers prefer Masbate City, so sailings here are thin and some are unserved since the pandemic. It is still the only jump-off for Bugui Point.
The port proper is at Calumpang. A fastcraft runs to Panay, and it is the jump-off for Jintotolo Island Lighthouse - neither is in this dataset yet.
1.5 km off the national highway.

A small coastal community at the northern tip of Masbate island, below the Spanish-era lighthouse. No pier, no facilities and no shop - bring what you need, and on the public boat expect to stay the night.

Sorsogon's port for Ticao. The crossing is short - MARINA measures it at 10.5 nautical miles - but San Jacinto at the far end is daytime-only, so the last useful sailing is earlier than Bulan's own hours suggest.

operators: Montenegro Shipping Lines; Kho Shipping Lines
notes: The town port has one ramp. The heavy traffic is at Mintac in the same municipality, a private Kho container terminal with the Cebu and Samar sailings.

Burias's southern port and a transit point rather than a destination - the Mobo and Pio Duran sailings are legs of one voyage that calls here. San Pascual, not Claveria, is where the island-hopping boats are booked.
Facing Naro Bay. The town jetty serves the fishing fleet and reaches Jamorawon, Deagan and Magcaraguit islands as well as Porta Vega.
Southern tip of the province. Recent public investment in access roads and seawalls; no operator listed as calling here.

ticketing: Bought at the pier before boarding
notes: Ticao's fastcraft pier and the busiest way on and off the island. PROVENANCE CONFLICT: this dataset files Lagundi under Monreal, a January 2026 provincial survey puts it in Batuan. Both are Ticao, so routing is unaffected, but the municipality is unresolved.
At Nin Bay. Better known to this app as the jump-off for Bat-ongan Cave, but it is also Masbate's link to Panay.
Van terminal for Mandaon and the west.

operators: Montenegro; Santa Clara; Penafrancia; Cokaliong; Trans-Asia
facilities: RoRo ramps; passenger terminal; cargo handling
notes: The province's base port and the one crossing you can almost always make: the harbour is sheltered behind Ticao Island and stays workable in weather that closes others. MARINA records six RoRo ramps. Check-in an hour before is Montenegro's stated policy.
Bus and UV Express for the mainland towns.

serves: Claveria (Burias); Pilar (Sorsogon); San Jacinto (Ticao); Pio Duran (Albay)
ticketing: Confirm at the pier - no online listing found
notes: Six kilometres south of Masbate City and a real passenger terminal, not only a fish port - it is where Kho's Burias and Sorsogon sailings actually leave from. Anyone arriving from Burias lands here, not in the city. Kho asks passengers aboard two hours before departure.
Where the Halea and island-hopping boats are arranged.

operators: Starhorse Shipping Lines; Kho Shipping Lines
notes: Camarines Sur's port for Burias and the approach most travellers actually use. Three sailings each way daily.
Roadside arch by NE Delos Santos Elementary School, then a 20 minute walk.

operators: Montenegro Shipping Lines; Kho Shipping Lines
notes: Mainland Bicol's main door to Masbate, with a sailing to Masbate City every two hours around the clock. SHALLOW DRAFT, which is why the bigger vessels do not call. Montenegro works a pier here reserved for its own ships, so check which berth your ticket is for.

operators: Santa Clara; Penafrancia; Montenegro; Kho Shipping Lines
notes: Albay's port for Masbate and much busier than this dataset used to show - MARINA lists eight sailings each way daily to Masbate City alone.
A working passenger and cargo port, not just the bangka pier for Nagarao. The Cebu sailings are intermittent - confirm before relying on one.
Where the Buntod sandbar boats are hired.
Quezon's port for Burias, on the Bondoc Peninsula. Worked as part of the San Andres - San Pascual - Pasacao circuit.

Ticao's fourth municipality. The port is operational but serves the fishing community - MARINA records Bulan to San Fernando as UNSERVED by RoRo, so it is not a passenger gateway. Known locally for coral rehabilitation and boat-making training.

DAYTIME NAVIGATION ONLY - MARINA certifies no night crossings here, whatever a timetable implies. Historically an anchorage and shipbuilding yard. Ticao's link to Sorsogon and the arrival pier for most divers.
The municipal tourism office here books the Burias island-hopping boats, and is the place to settle the boat and the fees before going to the pier. No ATM in the town.

operators: Starhorse Shipping Lines; Kho Shipping Lines
notes: The practical way into Burias and the jump-off for Animasola, Tinalisayan and Sombrero. Motorbancas here run mainly for tourism. There is no ATM in San Pascual - carry the whole trip in cash.
